Centers for Disease Control and Prevention [...] When a case tests positive for A(H5) at a public health laboratory but testing at CDC is not able to confirm A(H5) infection, per Council of State and Territorial Epidemiologists (CSTE) guidance, a case is reported as probable. In January 2025, CDC updated requirements. After a public health laboratory's first three cases of influenza A(H5) virus have been confirmed by CDC, subsequent detections by that laboratory can be considered confirmatory.
